quotes.text: If you contest a Visa compliance dispute, in addition to the applicable Stripe dispute fees, Stripe collects a 500 USD (or local equivalent) amount to cover the network costs associated with resolving Visa compliance disputes. Stripe refunds the 500 USD if you win the dispute.

Closing a Visa compliance dispute indicates that you don’t have any evidence to submit and are essentially dismissing the dispute, acknowledging it as lost. You aren’t charged the 500 USD Visa compliance network fee if you choose to close the dispute.
Stripe withdraws the 500 USD network fee from your balance asynchronously after you submit evidence, typically within 1-2 days.
If you attempt to submit evidence for a Visa compliance dispute without acknowledging the network fee, Stripe returns an error response and doesn’t submit your provided evidence.

findings: The November and May captures at the same canonical URL document the same Visa compliance dispute flow and test values (new lines 5-114; old lines 4-110). Closing through the close API acknowledges loss, avoids the Visa 500 USD network fee, and is irreversible; responding through update requires fee_acknowledged=true in enhanced evidence (new lines 42-56; old lines 41-55). Without acknowledgment, Stripe returns an error and does not submit the evidence (new line 100; old line 96). The status fee_acknowledged records acknowledgment, not a won dispute (new lines 74-98; old lines 72-94).
